judge_output.rationale: The claim is that quiescent galaxies show no galaxy-wide waste-heat excess over a stellar-population model, and that claim has been tested before with other data. The Ĝ papers II–III (2014ApJ...792...27W, 2015ApJS..217...25G) set mid-IR limits on starlight reprocessing for ~1e5 galaxies using WISE broadband photometry. Ĝ V (2026arXiv260812458C) fitted SPS models with a Dyson-swarm component to 129 nearby galaxies and found none preferring the component, with median α<0.3% in quiescent non-AGN hosts. No listed work uses SPHEREx R~35–130 spectra, a rest-frame 3.5–5 µm residual tracked through redshift to reject instrumental features, a 3.29 µm PAH veto, or a ~5×10^4 quiescent 2MASS XSC sample.

closest_prior.relation: SPS fitting with a Dyson-swarm component and injection-recovery on 129 nearby galaxies, including quiescent non-AGN hosts, with per-galaxy limits α<0.3% for T≳100 K; tests the same model-excess claim on a far smaller sample with broadband SEDs rather than SPHEREx spectra.

Recalibrated WISE extended-source photometry for ~1e5 galaxies finds none reprocessing >85% of starlight into the mid-IR; same population-level claim, but broadband colours only reach far higher reprocessing fractions and cannot separate a 3.5–5 µm excess from AGN dust.
Framework turning WISE mid-IR photometry into waste-heat limits, with a zeroth-order null result for Type III civilizations; photometric and much coarser than the card's spectral test.
Searches z<0.2 LoTSS galaxies for a mid-IR (22 µm) excess relative to the radio continuum (high q values), giving 2 unconfirmed candidates; different observable and wavelength.

judge_output.rationale: The card measures a rest-frame 3.5-5 um spectral excess over a fitted stellar-population model, resolved across SPHEREx channels, tracked in rest wavelength across redshift bins and paired with a 3.29 um PAH equivalent width. The Ĝ galaxy searches (2014ApJ...792...27W, 2015ApJS..217...25G, 2014ebi..confP5.93P) used WISE broadband colours. Those colours can show that a mid-IR excess exists but cannot give its spectral shape, separate PAH emission, or test whether a bump stays fixed in rest wavelength. Their reported limits also concern large reprocessing fractions (>50-85 per cent) in the mid-IR rather than a ~20 per cent near-IR bump, and no listed work has measured the card's spectroscopic quantity.

closest_prior.relation: Ĝ III searched ~1e5 galaxies for galaxy-spanning waste heat using recalibrated WISE extended-source photometry and colour selection, setting limits at >50-85 per cent reprocessing; it measured broadband mid-IR colours, not a rest-frame 3.5-5 um spectral excess with PAH separation.
Ĝ II set up the formalism and reported a zeroth-order WISE null result for Type III civilizations; it used broadband photometry and gave no spectral-shape or redshift-tracking test.
Ĝ first results catalogued 32,000 WISE extended sources and vetted the reddest by colour; this is a photometric excess search, not SPHEREx spectra fitted with stellar-population models.
proposes, not tested: a forecast of SPHEREx 3.3 um PAH measurements in nearby galaxies, with no waste-heat excess search.
